headline: Funding flows. Satellites multiply. Tests delay.
deck: This week sees significant funding for space startups and continued delays in hypersonic tests.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully closed a $190 million Series C round, boosting its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding is aimed at enhancing its co-orbital security capabilities, which are increasingly in demand as the U.S. military ramps up its focus on space defense. With DoD contracts now a headline feature, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the burgeoning market for space situational awareness.
stories.soWhat: The influx of capital shows that defense is still a reliable revenue stream, even as the broader market grapples with uncertainty.

stories.head: ESA-China SMILE mission finally set for May launch
stories.body: After a decade of planning, the ESA-China SMILE mission is scheduled to launch on May 19 to study Earth's magnetosphere. This joint effort highlights the complexities of international collaboration in space, often slower than expected but crucial for scientific advancement. With a focus on understanding space weather, the mission could yield insights relevant to satellite operations and terrestrial technology.
stories.soWhat: If this mission succeeds, it might just justify the decade-long wait, but don’t hold your breath for immediate results.

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slip for third time
stories.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has been delayed for the third consecutive quarter, underscoring the challenges facing this high-stakes technology. With the Pentagon investing heavily in hypersonics, including a notable increase of $1.4 billion in the FY27 budget for space resilience, the repeated delays raise questions about the effectiveness of current development strategies. Meanwhile, competitors are likely taking notes as the U.S. struggles to keep pace.
stories.soWhat: This is becoming the poster child for defense project procrastination—let's hope they don’t run out of excuses.

watchlist.title: MinoSpace IPO could shake up satellite market
watchlist.body: With MinoSpace seeking $736 million in its IPO, the move could intensify competition in the satellite sector, especially among Chinese manufacturers.

watchlist.title: Virgin Galactic's commercial flights on the horizon
watchlist.body: Virgin Galactic insists it will begin commercial flights this year, which could finally provide a revenue stream after years of delays.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris tactical bid heats up
watchlist.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris for a tactical SDA constellation could set new standards in defense satellite architecture.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program indicates sustained demand for its data solutions in military applications.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
